title: Ebola Spotlight - Emerging Infectious Diseases journal - CDC
content: Emerging Infectious Disease journal ISSN: 1080-6059 Ebola Spotlight Ebola disease is caused by infection with an orthoebolavirus. There are six identified orthoebolavirus species, four of which are known to cause disease in humans. Ebola is caused by infection with a virus of the family Filoviridae , genus Orthoebolavirus. These viruses can cause disease in humans and nonhuman primates (monkeys, gorillas, and chimpanzees). First discovered in 1976 near the Ebola River in what is now the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Ebola outbreaks have appeared sporadically in Africa. The natural reservoir host of orthoebolavirus remains unknown. However, based on evidence and the nature of similar viruses, researchers believe that the virus is animal-borne and that bats are the most likely reservoir. Emerging Infectious Diseases has published many articles on Ebola. The journal published its first Ebola article in 1995, volume 1, issue number 3. Reemergence of Ebola Virus in Africa . One orthoebolavirus species, Ebola Bundibugyo virus , has been linked to a 2026 outbreak in the DRC and Uganda.
